domain: Cold email outreach (UK, B2B), sent through the customer's own Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace mailbox
summary: Outreach is sent via Microsoft Graph POST /users/{mailbox}/sendMail or the Gmail API, through the customer's OWN tenant, from their own address, into their own Sent Items. Sending through ODoutreach IS sending from Outlook. This single fact changes the domain requirements materially: there is no second sending domain, so SPF already aligns and DMARC passes on SPF alignment alone. The customer needs ZERO DNS changes. The unavoidable ask is Entra admin consent - identity, not DNS.
supersession_note: Section 6 of the prose brief (30 July) recommends building a Sending Domain Readiness Gate that verifies SPF/DKIM/DMARC by live DNS lookup before allowing a send. That recommendation was written BEFORE the 6 August transport finding and is largely moot for the Graph/Gmail path, where authentication is inherited from the customer's existing corporate mail setup. It remains valid for any send that does NOT go through a connected mailbox. The prose brief has not been edited; this field records the supersession so the stale recommendation is not implemented by mistake.

email_authentication.note: SPF/DKIM/DMARC and alignment. Researched 2026-07-30 from cited sources, then verified 2026-08-06 against the actual transport. Key fact: DMARC passes if EITHER SPF or DKIM aligns; Graph sending aligns SPF, so DMARC passes with or without a published DMARC record. Exchange signs as <tenant>.onmicrosoft.com without custom DKIM, so DKIM alignment fails - this is not fatal. Custom DKIM and DMARC make it better, not possible.

link_alignment_and_phishing_heuristics.note: The ACTUAL root cause of the 2026 quarantine incident. Unsubscribe links and the open-tracking pixel pointed at the ODoutreach app domain while From: was the customer's domain - the textbook phishing pattern. This causes per-message quarantine; sustained quarantine plus complaints then degrades reputation, which is why it presented as domain damage. Note the ambiguity that caused confusion: 'domain mismatch' means DMARC alignment in the protocol sense, and links-not-matching-sender in the everyday sense. Only the first is an authentication failure.

volume_warmup_and_throttling.note: Industry norm is 4-6 mailboxes per sending domain at 40-50/day each. ODoutreach enforces 5 mailboxes at 30/day - MORE conservative than the standard, and correct. The volume logic was never the problem. A 30-day warm-up from zero is required for a new mailbox or domain.

uk_pecr_and_gdpr.note: PECR Regulation 22 plus UK GDPR. The distinction that matters is the recipient's LEGAL STRUCTURE, not whether they are 'a business': corporate subscribers (limited companies, LLPs, public bodies) need no prior consent; individual subscribers (sole traders, unincorporated partnerships, personal addresses) do. A one-person limited company falls under the carve-out; a sole trader does not. NOT LEGAL ADVICE - the prose brief says to confirm with a solicitor before relying on this commercially, and that confirmation has NOT been obtained. Recorded as an open item in SCOPE.md section 6.

deliverability_thresholds.note: Complaint rate below 0.1% and never reaching 0.3%; bounce rate below 2% overall (Gmail reputation review at 2%, Microsoft 365 throttles at 1.5%, Yahoo tolerates ~2.5%). KNOWLEDGE is Working. Automated enforcement is NOT built - bounce/complaint auto-halt is Phase 4 and explicitly out of scope for August. Hard-bounce suppression IS live and enabled.

domain_reputation_recovery.note: Diagnose via Google Postmaster Tools and blacklist checks, stop sending, re-warm from zero over 4-6 weeks, reintroduce cautiously. Retire rather than recover if on multiple major blacklists with delisting refused, or if 6-8 weeks of clean warm-up shows no improvement. Standing up a fresh correctly-configured domain takes 3-4 weeks. Does not gate a send in this product because the customer's own mailbox is the transport.

non_negotiables.requirement: Every sending domain must have SPF, DKIM and DMARC, and the From: domain must align with SPF or DKIM. DMARC passes if EITHER aligns.
non_negotiables.applies_here: Satisfied inherently by the Graph/Gmail transport - the customer's existing SPF already authorises Microsoft's or Google's IPs, or they could not send mail at all today.

non_negotiables.requirement: Bulk senders (5,000+/day to one provider) are subject to the full bulk-sender rules. Enforced by Google and Yahoo since 2024 and by Microsoft since 5 May 2025; Gmail escalated to permanent rejections in November 2025.
non_negotiables.applies_here: Not currently reached - 5 mailboxes at 30/day is 150/day per workspace.

non_negotiables.requirement: Spam complaint rate must stay below 0.1% and must never reach 0.3%. Bounce rate must stay below 2%.
non_negotiables.applies_here: Hard-bounce suppression is live. Automated complaint/bounce auto-halt is NOT built (Phase 4).

non_negotiables.requirement: A functional opt-out must be present and honoured, and opt-outs processed within 2 days. List-Unsubscribe must be present and functional.
non_negotiables.applies_here: Satisfied by the mailto: rail plus a visible plain-English opt-out line; reply ingestion auto-suppresses via classifyOptOutReply. Gated in code - see irreversible_actions.

non_negotiables.requirement: Never send cold email from the client's primary business domain; use a dedicated secondary domain or subdomain. A subdomain does NOT inherit the parent's SPF/DKIM/DMARC and needs its own.
non_negotiables.applies_here: PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED for this architecture and the most important nuance in this file. This rule protects a domain's reputation from cold-outreach damage. ODoutreach deliberately sends from the customer's real business mailbox, which is what makes zero-DNS onboarding possible - and it is also precisely the exposure this rule warns about. The mitigating facts: volume is low (30/day/mailbox), the transport is the customer's own tenant, and the phishing signal that caused the incident has been removed. The residual risk is real and should be stated to any customer rather than glossed: heavy or careless outreach from a primary business domain can still damage ordinary business mail. The industry rule is not wrong; this architecture trades it for onboarding, knowingly.

non_negotiables.requirement: UK: corporate subscribers (limited companies, LLPs, public bodies) may be emailed without prior consent. Individual subscribers (sole traders, unincorporated partnerships, personal addresses) require consent or soft opt-in.
non_negotiables.applies_here: NOT ENFORCED IN CODE. The contact-import pipeline cannot distinguish a sole trader from a limited company. Flagged in the prose brief as a genuine billable feature with a compliance justification. Not yet scoped into any phase.

non_negotiables.requirement: Truthful identification is always required regardless of recipient type: real sender name, real company identity, genuine reply address, no deceptive subject lines.
non_negotiables.applies_here: Satisfied - mail comes from the customer's own named mailbox and replies return to it.

irreversible_actions.action: Dispatch an outreach email to a real prospect through a connected mailbox
irreversible_actions.gate: src/server/email/outbound/execute-one.ts - executeOutboundSend routes any row with a mailboxIdentityId to sendViaConnectedMailboxOrFail, which has NO ESP fallback: if the connected mailbox cannot send, the row fails rather than silently rerouting. Layered with evaluateSuppression (suppression-guard.ts), the client send-governance decision, and the per-mailbox daily cap in sending-policy.ts.
irreversible_actions.evidence: src/server/outreach/suppression-guard.test.ts returns skipped_missing_email on null/empty/undefined rather than proceeding; src/lib/clients/client-send-governance.test.ts asserts 'blocks a non-allowlisted recipient even if client is LIVE_PROSPECT-approved' and 'blocks non-allowlisted recipients when client is ONBOARDING'; src/server/mailbox/sending-policy.test.ts asserts errorCode MAILBOX_DAILY_CAP. All verified passing 2026-08-09.

irreversible_actions.action: Send an outreach email that carries no working opt-out, or whose links point at a domain that does not match the sender (the 2026 quarantine root cause)
irreversible_actions.gate: src/lib/unsubscribe/one-click-readiness.ts resolves the opt-out rail as hosted-on-the-client's-aligned-domain OR mailto, and returns none when neither is available. Commit a8d777c removed the app-domain fallback entirely and stopped importing resolvePublicBaseUrl into that module so it cannot return by accident.
irreversible_actions.evidence: src/lib/unsubscribe/one-click-readiness.test.ts asserts 'returns none when neither rail is available', 'returns none when the sending address is not a usable opt-out target', and the regression test 'does NOT read the app base URL from the environment'. Verified passing 2026-08-09.

irreversible_actions.action: Mark an outreach email as SENT when no mail actually left the system
irreversible_actions.gate: src/server/email/outbound/prospect-send-transport-guard.ts - evaluateProspectSendTransport() refuses any row that carries a contactId (i.e. is addressed to a real prospect) but has no mailboxIdentityId. Wired into execute-one.ts immediately before the mailbox/legacy branch: on block it calls markFailed(row.id, 'NO_SENDING_MAILBOX', reason), so the row goes to FAILED with a diagnosable error instead of falling through to the mock and being recorded as SENT.
irreversible_actions.evidence: CLOSED 2026-08-09 on branch fix/refuse-mock-send-for-prospect-rows. src/server/email/outbound/prospect-send-transport-guard.test.ts - 8 tests. Fail-closed cases: blocks a prospect row with no mailbox; blocks for EVERY value of EMAIL_PROVIDER including unset, mock and resend (the guard never consults it, so setting the flag cannot reopen the hole); blocks on an empty-string mailbox id, not only null. Non-regression cases: allows a prospect row that HAS a mailbox; allows legacy/platform mail, which carries no contactId, so the pluggable provider stack is untouched. Verified by running the full gate on 2026-08-09: lint exit 0, typecheck exit 0, 1836 tests passed across 214 files (baseline on this branch was 1828/213 - no regressions).
irreversible_actions.known_limitation: The pure decision function is tested; the four-line wiring in execute-one.ts is not covered by an automated test, because executeOutboundSend needs a database and the unit suite is deliberately DB-free. The wiring was verified by reading it. An integration test belongs in execute-one.integration.test.ts when a database is available.
irreversible_actions.design_note: Deliberately NOT behind a feature flag, against the local convention that send-path changes ship flag-off. Justification: this guard can only ever intercept a row that was about to be handed to the legacy ESP stack, which in production is the mock and delivers nothing. It therefore cannot turn a real send into a non-send - it converts a silent fake success into a visible failure. A flag defaulting to off would leave the defect live.

irreversible_actions.action: Send to a recipient on the do-not-contact list belonging to a related domain (bt.com listed, bteurope.com emailed)
irreversible_actions.evidence: VERIFIED OPEN. suppression-guard.ts matches domains on an exact unique-key lookup, so a DNC entry for one corporate domain does not cover its sibling domains. The client raised this directly and it is a live compliance exposure, not a theoretical one. Scheduled as Phase 2 (eTLD+1 normalisation via the Public Suffix List, auto-block on strong signals such as a shared Entra tenant id, suggest-only on weak brand-token matches). Exact-match suppression itself works correctly and is tested.
irreversible_actions.what_would_close_it: Phase 2, estimated 6 naive / 18 Tier P days. Sequenced deliberately ahead of the domain-verification work.

partial_gate_2026_08_22.what_was_built: A suppressed domain now covers its SUBDOMAINS. src/lib/normalize.ts suppressionDomainCandidates expands the recipient domain into itself plus each parent (newsletter.bt.com -> [newsletter.bt.com, bt.com]); src/server/outreach/suppression-guard.ts evaluateSuppression matches any of them. Splits on label boundaries, not string suffix, so notbt.com and bt.com.evil.net are still NOT blocked. Stops at two labels so a stray 'com' row cannot blackhole every send.
partial_gate_2026_08_22.fail_closed_test: src/server/outreach/suppression-guard.subdomain.test.ts — 8 tests. Seen RED first against the old exact-match lookup: the three subdomain cases failed while the four over-blocking guards already passed. Green after the fix. Plus 7 pure-function tests in src/lib/normalize.test.ts.
partial_gate_2026_08_22.what_is_STILL_UNGATED: RELATED COMPANY DOMAINS — the thing this register entry actually names. Whether do-not-contact for bt.com also covers bteurope.com cannot be derived from the string and is a client business rule, not an engineering inference. Until Greg decides it, there is no gate for this action and fail_closed_test stays false. The block is correct and must remain.

irreversible_actions.action: Ramp a brand-new mailbox straight to full volume instead of warming it up over 30 days
irreversible_actions.gate: src/lib/mailboxes/mailbox-warmup.ts implements the graduated ramp, and the flat per-mailbox daily cap in sending-policy.ts (30/day, 5 mailboxes) applies unconditionally and is tested.
irreversible_actions.evidence: CLOSED - and it was already closed before this session; the earlier record was stale. Verified live on 2026-08-09 against production: `az webapp config appsettings list --name app-opensdoors-outreach-prod --resource-group rg-opensdoors-outreach-prod --query "[?name=='MAILBOX_WARMUP_RAMP']"` returns value 'on', which is the exact string isWarmupRampEnabled() requires. The August roadmap and the engagement notes both recorded this flag as OFF; that is no longer true and those documents should not be trusted on this point. Fail-closed proof in src/lib/mailboxes/mailbox-warmup.test.ts: warmupDailyCap(30, -3) === 5 (clock skew is treated as day 0, the MOST restrictive value, not the least) and warmupDailyCap(30, NaN) === 5 (unknown age also collapses to the base cap); 'never exceeds the mailbox's configured steady cap' asserts the ceiling holds at 30, 20 and custom caps. An unknown or nonsensical input yields the lowest permitted volume, which is what fail-closed means for a ceiling.
irreversible_actions.caveat: The ramp is activated by a flag that DEFAULTS TO OFF, so the gate is fail-closed in its logic but fail-open in its activation: turning MAILBOX_WARMUP_RAMP off silently returns every mailbox to its full configured cap on day one. The unconditional flat per-mailbox cap (30/day) still applies in that case and is separately tested, so the exposure is a missing graduated protection rather than unlimited sending. Re-verify this flag before relying on this entry.

Should MAILBOX_WARMUP_RAMP be enabled now? Greg's client email claims volume protection is active, which is not true while it is off.

Should the corporate-vs-sole-trader distinction be built into contact import? It is a real compliance gap and a billable feature, currently in no phase.

compensating_controls.for: Absent bounce measurement on the live mailbox send path
compensating_controls.finding: There are no provider delivery webhooks for Graph/Gmail sends, but bounce detection is NOT absent: src/server/mailbox/bounce-detection.ts parses NDR/DSN bounce-backs out of the connected mailbox during inbox sync and is wired into mailbox-inbox-sync.ts. It is gated by MAILBOX_BOUNCE_DETECTION_ENABLED, which DEFAULTS OFF and is absent from .env.example. A reported 0% bounce rate across ~1,209 sends is therefore much more likely to mean 'nothing is measuring' than 'delivery is clean'.
compensating_controls.control: Cap pilot volume hard while the bounce rate is unmeasured, and route the pilot through the controlled-pilot path (src/app/(app)/clients/controlled-pilot-send-actions.ts). Proposed cap: 20 sends per client per day, and no more than 10 per mailbox per day, for the first 10 working days.
compensating_controls.why_that_number: The domain brief's non-negotiable is a bounce rate below 2%. At 20 sends/day a single hard bounce is 5% of the day's volume and 0.5% of a 10-day pilot, so ONE bad address is visible by eye in the reply inbox without any measurement infrastructure at all — that is the point of the number. It also sits inside the product's own warm-up ramp (WARMUP_BASE_CAP 5, +5 every 5 days), so it does not fight the existing control, and inside the researched week-1 guidance of 5-10/day/mailbox.
compensating_controls.trigger_that_lifts_it: BOTH: (1) MAILBOX_BOUNCE_DETECTION_ENABLED=true in Azure App Service config, confirmed by observing at least one real NDR being detected and suppressed; and (2) a measured bounce rate below 2% over a minimum of 200 sends. Until both hold, volume is the substitute for measurement.
compensating_controls.cheaper_first_step: Turn MAILBOX_BOUNCE_DETECTION_ENABLED on. It is an env var on an already-built, already-tested path, not a webhook project.
